policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Official NIST reference page (initial publication 2025-01-21, subsequently updated through at least 2025-07-23) cataloging the congressional statutes (CHIPS and Science Act of 2022, National AI Initiative Act of 2020), America's AI Action Plan (July 2025), and Executive Orders (Jan 2025 EO 14179, rescinded Oct 2023 EO 14110, Dec 2020 EO 13960, Feb 2019 EO 13859) driving NIST's non-regulatory AI standards, testbed, cybersecurity, and evaluation activities. As a summary webpage, it imposes no direct legal obligations or enforcement mechanisms.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: This mandates catalog reflects a close three-way balance led by innovation_enablement, which runs across every cited statute and executive action via technical standards, testbeds, research infrastructure (NAIRR), open-source/open-weight encouragement, AI adoption, and reviewing regulatory obstacles from rescinded EO 14110. Innovation_enablement narrowly edges out national_security and economic_competitiveness, which are strongly articulated in the 2025 executive actions through military/intelligence data centers, critical infrastructure cybersecurity, biosecurity, frontier national security risk evaluations, and sustaining America's global AI dominance. Fundamental_rights (free speech, testing for bias in training data) and consumer_public_safety (safe and trustworthy AI) appear as smaller supporting rationales.
